ask: Schedule this for Tuesday 9am on LinkedIn: 'We are hiring two support engineers. Remote, EU hours.'

arguments.content: We are hiring two support engineers. Remote, EU hours.

steps.why: Their own text with a time is the yes, but the post is still saved as a plain draft first.
Puts it on the review list, which gives it a content_fingerprint.
Read the row again for its content_fingerprint.
One yes, so approve-post: its result carries scheduled_time (UTC) to read back in the brand's clock. Wall clock in, no Z, no offset, no timezone unless the user named a place.

say: Scheduled for Acme: Tue Nov 17, 9:00 am (New York) on LinkedIn.
never: A UTC offset or a Z on the time.
A weekday copied from an example: work it out from the date.
Retrying or calling publish-post after self_approval_not_allowed: in a team brand someone else must approve a post the user sent for review.
